paper.title: Empowering VLMs for Few-Shot Multimodal Time Series Classification via Tailored Agentic Reasoning
paper.central_claim: MarsTSC, a Generator-Reflector-Modifier agentic framework with a self-evolving bullet-level knowledge bank (plus a cautious test-time update), lets VLMs classify few-shot multimodal time series better than classical, deep and foundation-model baselines on 12 UCR/UEA datasets across 5 VLM backbones, even competing with full-shot baselines.

evidence.quote: introduces a self-evolving knowledge bank as a dynamic context iteratively refined via reflective agentic reasoning
evidence.support_explanation: Central object: a non-weight knowledge bank used as VLM context and refined from feedback.

evidence.quote: existing approaches rely on static context that fail to automatically evolve with the few-shot training samples
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: static context.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we structure the knowledge bank as feature bullet points to enable atomic updates
evidence.support_explanation: Design response to context collapse.

evidence.quote: Each bullet is maintained by a unique ID and a tag counter (useful, neutral, useless).
evidence.support_explanation: Per-entry usage statistics.

evidence.quote: We compute a normalized Fisher Score to evaluate pairwise class separability, establishing explicit decision thresholds for the most discriminative descriptors between each pair of classes.
evidence.support_explanation: Statistical warm-up from labelled few-shot samples.

evidence.quote: the Reflector tags the cited feature bullet points as either useful, neutral, or useless based on their contribution to the correct or incorrect decision
evidence.support_explanation: Tags are LLM judgments against ground truth, not memory-on/off counterfactuals.

evidence.quote: the Modifier is restricted to performing updates bullet by bullet
evidence.support_explanation: Edit vocabulary ADD/MODIFY/DELETE per bullet.

evidence.quote: We find that naive self-improvement that directly prompts the model to refine the knowledge bank leads to overwriting the entire content.
evidence.support_explanation: Claim about monolithic rewriting; no rewrite-baseline comparison is reported in Tables 1-8.

evidence.quote: ensures that only statistically recurrently supported temporal patterns are permanently consolidated into the knowledge bank
evidence.support_explanation: Counter-based discard; no ablation of the discarding mechanism.

evidence.quote: Modifier applies verified updates to the knowledge bank to prevent context collapse
evidence.support_explanation: Edits are 'verified' only by the Reflector's diagnosis; no held-out accept/reject test of training-stage edits is described.

evidence.quote: optimizes the knowledge bank on the few-shot training and validation samples to gradually refine the task contexts in a dynamic manner
evidence.support_explanation: Validation samples serve as extra reflection data rather than a held-out gate.

evidence.quote: Another purpose of our two-pass generation design is to provide a pseudo-supervisory signal for test-time refinement.
evidence.support_explanation: Test-time update is driven by the model's own second-pass prediction.

evidence.quote: Prototype knowledge is frozen during testing and the Modifier is not allowed to operate on it, thereby preventing contamination of the core knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Anchor tier retained from labelled training.

evidence.quote: refers to newly extracted knowledge at test-time. It is temporarily stored in a buffer and does not participate in classification decisions.
evidence.support_explanation: Candidate tier = quarantine before promotion by counters.

evidence.quote: so as to simulate a real-world deployment scenario where test samples arrive sequentially in a streaming manner

signatures.object: Knowledge bank K of feature bullets (intra-class features, inter-class features with Fisher-score thresholds, mistakes to avoid, distinguishing strategies, dataset background) used as VLM context; baseline = warm-up bank before refinement.
signatures.information: Generator sees query plot, bank, dataset info and sample statistics; Reflector additionally sees the ground-truth label and retrieved hard-positive / hard-negative exemplars; Modifier sees the reflection and the bank. Few-shot train and validation samples (3 per class each) are both used.
signatures.operation: Generate with cited bullets -> reflect (tag cited bullets useful/neutral/useless; contrastive root-cause insight) -> bullet-level ADD/MODIFY/DELETE -> discard bullets whose useless tags exceed a threshold.
signatures.conditions: tau_drop = 10% of training steps; number of training rounds not given.
signatures.feedback: Ground-truth labels of few-shot training/validation samples.
signatures.selection_rule: No held-out acceptance test per edit; counter-based discard and restricted edit vocabulary.
signatures.selection_data: Same few-shot train+val samples are used for proposing and tagging; no separate gate set.
signatures.persistence: Bank persists (token count stabilises) and becomes the 'prototype' tier at test time.
signatures.later_use: Generator cites bullets when classifying test samples of the same dataset.
signatures.claimed_effect: Warm-up-only to full-minus-test-update: e.g. ArrowHead 0.543 -> 0.691, ECG200 0.640 -> 0.770, Fish 0.600 -> 0.726.
signatures.failure_boundary: LLM-judged tags; no rewrite-baseline; modifier not independently verified.

signatures.object: Test-time extension of the same bank with Reference and Candidate tiers; prototype tier frozen.
signatures.information: Unlabeled test stream in random order, no labels; two-pass generation yields a pseudo-label.
signatures.operation: Pass-1 -> pass-2 re-check -> treat pass-2 as pseudo-label; agreement => positive instance, disagreement => negative for pass-1 class -> Reflector/Modifier (no DELETE) -> candidate counters (+1/-1) -> promote at >= 5, remove at <= -2, demote reference below promote threshold.
signatures.output: Candidate/reference bullets added to the bank.
signatures.conditions: Bank reset at each run; thresholds set heuristically.
signatures.feedback: Self-consistency of the VLM; Reflector usefulness tags.
signatures.persistence: Within a run only; reset before each run.
signatures.later_use: Reference tier is shown to the Generator as 'suspicious but informative'; candidates not used.
signatures.claimed_effect: Full vs w/o update: Dodger 0.884 vs 0.812, ArrowHead 0.766 vs 0.691; SCP1 0.697 vs 0.717.
signatures.failure_boundary: Both passes wrong or pass-2 over-corrects; Tables 3 and 8 disagree for the same ablation.

gap.author_gap: Existing VLM-based time-series methods use static context that does not evolve with few-shot samples and lack agentic reasoning that grounds rationales in discriminative evidence.
gap.checked_gap: A real, concrete setting (few-shot TSC with VLMs), but the mechanism is largely an ACE-style generate-reflect-curate playbook transplanted to a new vertical; the domain-specific additions (Fisher-score warm-up, contrastive hard pos/neg reflection, test-time tiered pseudo-label update) are not isolated individually.
gap.lineage: In-context / template reasoning for time series (Zhou 2025a) -> ACE and A-mem style evolving memory for code/math -> MarsTSC (bullet-level bank for TSC with tiered test-time update); agentic TS systems (TimeXL, MERIT, TSci) are the domain neighbours.
gap.closest_adjacent: ACE (generator/reflector/curator on a bullet playbook) is the evident ancestor but is not run as a baseline; TimeXL and TimeOmni-VL are the TS neighbours (TimeOmni-VL evaluated in an unfaithful configuration).
gap.residue: Few-shot exemplar prompting with the same 3-shot data, generic ACE-style bank and rewrite-based curation are not compared, so which components create the gain remains open.
gap.stakes: Few-shot supervision is scarce in healthcare/industrial TSC; interpretable rationales are valued.
gap.method_response: Evolve a typed bullet bank from labelled few-shot feedback, then adapt cautiously at test time with a quarantine/promotion mechanism.
gap.remaining_gap: Admission gating of training-stage edits, independent referee for test-time updates, cost accounting.
unresolved: Original text of ACE / TimeXL not fixed in this batch; novelty relative to ACE is judged from the paper's own description.

claims.text: MarsTSC outperforms classical, deep and foundation-model TS baselines in the 3-shot setting on 12 datasets.
claims.setting: UCR/UEA, accuracy, k=3 train + 3 val per class, Gemini-3.1-pro, 3 runs.
claims.baseline_control: DrCIF, HIVE-COTE 2.0, TimesNet, Autoformer, PatchTST, GPT4TS, MOMENT; extended DTW, COSCO, TapNet, TimeOmni-VL on 5 datasets.
claims.selection_vs_test: Few-shot train/val from original train; default test.
claims.result: Best on 7/12, second on the remaining 5 (HIVE-COTE 2.0 best on 4, GPT4TS on 1); means without std; small test sets.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Highest accuracy on 7 of 12 chosen datasets in 3-shot, with an information/model-scale advantage over trained-from-scratch baselines; not superior on every dataset.

claims.text: The reflective train-time refinement and cautious test-time update, not just a stronger foundation model, produce the gain.
claims.baseline_control: Direct VLM inference; warm-up-only bank; w/o test update; w/o 2-pass; m-vote scaling.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same few-shot data; test on default test split.
claims.result: Warm-up-only bank vs full: +0.04 to +0.23 (e.g. ArrowHead 0.543 -> 0.766); refine alone +0.00 to +0.20; test update 0 to +0.07 (SCP1 -0.02). Warm-up bank alone already far above direct inference (Fish 0.143 vs 0.600).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Refinement and test-time update each add accuracy on most datasets beyond the warm-up bank; much of the gain over direct inference comes from the warm-up bank built from labelled samples.

claims.text: With only 3 shots MarsTSC competes with full-shot trained baselines and works across 5 VLMs.
claims.baseline_control: Baselines trained with k to full shot.
claims.result: Authors state 'competitive and in most cases outperforms'; Fish full-shot MOMENT 0.914 and DistalPhalanxTW full-shot 0.727 exceed MarsTSC.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Competitive with several larger-data baselines on many datasets; not uniformly better.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A bullet-level knowledge bank refined from 3-shot labelled feedback and cautiously updated at test time raises accuracy over the warm-up bank and over direct Gemini-3.1-pro inference on most of 12 UCR/UEA datasets (author-reported, 3 runs, default test splits), and gives the best 3-shot accuracy on 7 of 12 datasets versus the listed baselines.
assessment.not_supported: Superiority over all baselines on every dataset; that bullet-level atomic edits, discarding or the tier structure individually prevent collapse; that gains hold when baselines receive equal context/model scale.
unresolved: Comparison with a generic ACE-style bank

G.reason: Real, concrete limitation (static context in few-shot VLM TSC, no grounded rationales) with TS-specific neighbours named, but the ACE-style ancestor is not compared and the novelty is partly a domain port; residual bottleneck beyond 'ours is dynamic' is not bounded.

M.reason: Operations, information visibility and rationale are clear and TS-specific: contrastive reflection against hard exemplars, Fisher-score thresholds, per-bullet counters, quarantine/promotion tiers. Distinguishing predictions versus generic rewrite curation are stated but not tested.

X.reason: Edit vocabulary, tag counters, tiers, thresholds, reset and frozen prototype tier are all specified with prompts. Missing: number of training rounds, retrieval of hard exemplars, held-out admission test for training edits, rollback; thresholds heuristic.

E.measurement.reason: Accuracy on standard UCR/UEA default test splits with three runs; trivial baselines (majority class) and the TimeOmni-VL configuration are weak points, and the 12 datasets were chosen without a stated rule.

E.causality.reason: Stage ablation on all 12 datasets (warm-up only / no test update / full), direct inference, 2-pass ablation and an m-vote compute control isolate refinement and test update. Gaps: no ACE/rewrite or in-context exemplar baseline, no ablation of Fisher init, hard-pos/neg contrast, discarding or tiers, Tables 3 and 8 disagree, baselines lack the context and model scale.

E.holdout.reason: Few-shot train/val are sampled from the original train split and the default test split is untouched; test-time adaptation on the test stream is declared and ablated; bank reset per run. Remaining: public-data contamination of the base VLM unaudited, validation used as extra reflection data, dataset subset unspecified, hyperparameters heuristic.

E.statistics.reason: Three seeded runs and shot/seed error bars on three datasets, but no std or tests in the main tables, small test sets (73-175 samples common) and table inconsistencies.

E.cost.reason: A compute-matched voting control and bank token count exist, but no per-sample VLM calls, tokens, latency or cost for training and the two-pass/reflection/modifier test-time pipeline, while baselines are cheap trained models.
